question: How do props work in Vue 3?
shortAnswer: Declared via defineProps; one-way down from parent to child; validated/typed optionally.
detailedAnswer: Mutating props is an anti-pattern—emit events or use v-model. Defaults via withDefaults.

question: How do emits work?
shortAnswer: declare via defineEmits; child triggers events; parent listens with @event.
detailedAnswer: Prefer explicit emit declarations for documentation and validation. Payload typing matters in TS.
example:
const emit = defineEmits<{ save: [id: number] }>()
emit('save', 1)

question: How does v-model work on components?
shortAnswer: Default model is modelValue prop + update:modelValue emit; can define multiple v-models.
detailedAnswer: Enables two-way binding ergonomics while staying explicit under the hood.

question: Props validation — runtime vs TypeScript?
shortAnswer: Runtime props options validate in dev; TS validates at compile time—use both thoughtfully.
detailedAnswer: Runtime validators help JS consumers. Don't rely on runtime alone in TS apps.

question: Fallthrough attributes — what are they?
shortAnswer: Non-prop attributes fall onto the root element unless inheritAttrs: false.
detailedAnswer: Important for wrapper components—bind $attrs intentionally to the right element.

question: When to use prop drilling vs provide/inject vs Pinia?
shortAnswer: Shallow trees: props; sparse deep concerns: provide/inject; broad shared state: Pinia.
detailedAnswer: Prefer the simplest that stays clear.

question: Boolean props casting quirks?
shortAnswer: Presence of a boolean prop without value becomes true; be careful with string 'false'.
detailedAnswer: Prefer explicit :flag="false". Know attribute fallthrough behavior.

question: Design events for a complex picker component.
shortAnswer: Emit update:modelValue, change with full payload, and blur/focus when a11y needs; document payloads.
detailedAnswer: Don't emit redundant events. Keep names consistent with Vue style guide.

question: one-way data flow — why does Vue emphasize it?
shortAnswer: Predictable updates: parents own state; children request changes via events.
detailedAnswer: Two-way binding is sugar over this. Mutating props breaks the model.

question: How do you type v-model with TypeScript?
shortAnswer: Type modelValue and update:modelValue emit; or use defineModel in supported Vue versions.
detailedAnswer: defineModel simplifies boilerplate—know your Vue version.
